This hub brings together the definitions, use cases, comparisons, and resources that show what APM looks like in practice, starting with a live walkthrough below. What Is Agentic Performance Management? The clearest way to understand Agentic Performance Management is to see it in action. This session covers what it is, what it isn't, and where agents take on reconciliation, consolidation, and close work end to end. The Agentic Performance Management Playbook For a complete view of the category, the full playbook covers the four core principles, seven use cases with customer results, a governance framework, and an evaluation checklist for separating true APM from tools that only look the part. Download the Playbook See Agentic Performance Management on Your Books Book a Demo Understanding Agentic Performance Management Finance teams have spent years layering point solutions on top of an ERP: close management tools that coordinate people, consolidation software that reports after the fact, and copilots that answer questions without acting on them. None of these execute the underlying accounting work. Agentic Performance Management closes that gap. APM describes a coordinated system of specialized agents that operates on top of an existing ERP to independently complete multi-step accounting workflows, with traceability and human oversight built in. Rather than assisting a person through reconciliation, consolidation, or flux analysis, the agents perform the work directly and escalate only genuine exceptions for review. The result is a system that acts on the books rather than one that only describes them. This distinction matters because the categories APM gets compared to (ERP, EPM, RPA, and AI copilots) all play a different role in the accounting stack. Each is covered in more depth further down this page. Controllers and finance leaders shift from doing the work to reviewing it, reserving judgment for the decisions that actually need it. A continuous close APM treats "done" as a daily state rather than a month-end milestone. Agents validate, reconcile, and keep the books ready for close in near real time, which cuts down the scramble that typically defines the final days of a period. ERP-agnostic, multi-entity by design The platform works across multiple ERPs, entities, and currencies without a system migration, functioning as a control layer that unifies fragmented structures rather than replacing them. Human-in-the-loop governance Every action runs inside rules, thresholds, and approval paths defined in natural language. Teams decide when escalation is required and can access full documentation at any time.
